statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump urging AI talks with China
statements.quote: develop a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, the development of biological weapons, and other dangerous activities that threaten the lives of the American people and humanity writ large.
statements.context: The senators asked the President to raise AI safety directly with Xi Jinping at the summit planned for 24 September 2026, including by working with China on such an agreement.
statements.source_label: Letter PDF, Senate Commerce Committee website
statements.reason: The letter Kaine signed says frontier AI development could enable bioweapons and other activities that threaten humanity as a whole, which is level A under ruling 1.

statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump urging AI talks with China
statements.quote: We encourage you to embrace these challenges because the stakes are existential, and our response must match the moment.
statements.context: The letter compares AI talks with China to nuclear arms control between the United States and the Soviet Union, calling AI a technology that poses an existential threat.
statements.source_label: Letter PDF, Senate Commerce Committee website
statements.reason: The letter calls the stakes of advanced AI existential, in a paragraph likening it to nuclear weapons.

statements.venue: Letter from 17 senators to President Trump urging AI talks with China
statements.quote: The experts building frontier AI models have also been raising concerns for some time that the capabilities of AI models may soon accelerate beyond our ability to understand or control them.
statements.context: The letter cites a July 2026 call by over 1,300 employees of frontier AI companies and, two sentences later, says "We should take these warnings seriously."
statements.source_label: Letter PDF, Senate Commerce Committee website
statements.reason: The letter relays experts' warning of loss of control and endorses it, without saying the loss would be permanent, so B rather than A.

statements.quote: I do think we don't need to be just complete doomsdayers about it.
statements.context: Kaine was reacting to President Trump calling warnings about AI danger a hoax; just before this he said "I don't think President Trump really knows what he's talking about."
statements.source_label: Fox News Digital, republished by WFMD
statements.reason: His only own-words remark found on AI danger neither names a catastrophic risk nor dismisses one; he rejects both Trump's dismissal and full doom.
